{"id":"zstreamer-467","title":"Runtime node loading","description":"Support loading and unloading processing nodes at runtime rather than having all nodes active from boot. When a dynamic router encounters a buffer type that needs a specific decoder/processor, instantiate that node on demand. When the stream ends or changes type, tear it down to reclaim memory.

This is critical for resource-constrained devices where you might support 10 different codecs but only need 1-2 active at any time.

Key challenges:
- Zephyr devices are typically statically defined via DTS — need a mechanism for deferred or dynamic instantiation
- Thread creation/destruction lifecycle management
- Graph topology changes while pipeline is running (thread-safe routing table updates)
- Memory management: pre-allocate node structs and stacks, or use dynamic allocation
- Integration with dynamic routing: router must be notified when new nodes become available

Possible approaches:
- Pre-define all possible nodes in DTS but defer their init (start threads on demand)
- Use Zephyr device_init_deferred or manual init gating
- Pool of generic worker threads that get assigned different process() callbacks
- Node registry pattern: nodes register their supported types, router queries registry
","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"epic","owner":"sharonthecreator@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-03-12T23:51:12Z","created_by":"Sharon Naim","updated_at":"2026-03-12T23:51:12Z"}

{"description":"A pre-allocated single-thread worker pool that handles dynamic node dispatch at runtime. Instead of spawning/destroying threads per codec, a single dedicated worker thread picks up jobs from a queue — each job is a different processing function (e.g. MP3 demux, Matroska demux, PCM passthrough).

## Design

**Work queue pattern:**
- One persistent thread with a pre-allocated stack (like Zephyr k_work_q)
- A queue of work items, each carrying: buffer pointer, process() callback, context pointer
- The worker thread dequeues and executes the appropriate process() for each buffer
- Memory for work items is pre-allocated from a fixed pool (k_mem_slab or static array) — no runtime malloc

**How it integrates with dynamic routing:**
1. Dynamic router inspects buffer type
2. Looks up the registered process() callback for that type
3. Submits a work item: {buffer, process_fn, node_ctx} to the worker queue
4. Worker thread executes process_fn(node_ctx, buffer) and forwards the result

**Pre-reserved memory:**
- Worker thread stack: single ZSTREAMER_THREAD_STACK_SIZE allocation at compile time
- Work item pool: fixed-size slab of N work item structs (configurable via Kconfig)
- Node contexts: each registered "virtual node" gets a pre-allocated context struct with its state, but no dedicated thread or stack
- This means 10 different demux nodes share 1 thread + 1 stack, with only their context structs taking separate memory

**Advantages over thread-per-node:**
- Deterministic memory usage — all reserved at compile time
- No thread create/destroy overhead at runtime
- Scales to many node types without linear stack cost (10 nodes × 2KB = 20KB saved vs 1 × 2KB shared)
- Natural backpressure via queue depth

**Key considerations:**
- Sequential processing: only one demux runs at a time on the worker thread — acceptable if demux is not the bottleneck
- Priority: worker thread priority must be chosen carefully (probably same as normal node threads)
- If parallel demux is ever needed, can extend to a thread pool (N workers) without changing the API
"}
